robot.name: Boston Dynamics Electric Atlas
robot.status_notes: Production-ready product version announced at CES 2026; Boston Dynamics says 2026 deployments are committed for Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind, while AP reports Hyundai factory deployment by 2028. Public CES stage demo was remotely piloted.

currentness.currentness_notes: Current production-version Atlas product as of 2026-05-16; scored as pilot because public evidence supports field testing/scheduled fleets, not open commercial availability or scaled customer metrics.

battery.original_value: Rechargeable and swappable 1.4 kWh lithium-ion battery
battery.notes: Official spec sheet also says the pack is rechargeable/swappable and supports 4 hr runtime under stated operating limits.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Official spec sheet/product page claim 56 total DoF, including 18 DoF per arm and 6 DoF per leg.

walking_speed.notes: Reported by robohub.app, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; Third-party aggregator listing (no official Boston Dynamics source states a speed); unit is walking/top speed unspecified.

hands.description: Multi-purpose industrial gripper with tactile sensing and 14 kg grip strength.
hands.force_feedback: Tactile feedback claimed in official spec sheet.

items: 2D/3D vision model inputs described by Boston Dynamics for behavior generation
human detection for fenceless safety claims

compute.description: Integrated compute not publicly specified; official materials emphasize manipulation, motion-control, and perception software rather than chip-level compute.

actuators.description: Boston Dynamics describes Atlas as fully electric; official public sources reviewed did not provide actuator model or torque specs.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Official specs claim a 50 kg payload, 2-DoF tactile grippers with 14 kg grip strength, and industrial applications such as part sequencing, machine tending, and order fulfillment.
caveats: No cycle-time, success-rate, or failure-rate benchmark was found.
Gripper strength and payload are company specs, not independent lab measurements.
Public demo evidence should not be generalized beyond observed/claimed industrial tasks.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Boston Dynamics says Atlas supports autonomous operation with optional teleoperation, intent selection, and policy learning; AP says the CES stage demo was remotely piloted.
caveats: The most visible public CES demonstration was reportedly remotely piloted.
No independent autonomy benchmark, intervention rate, or raw task log was found.
Treat autonomy claims as industrial-pilot evidence, not proof of broad general-purpose autonomy.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Electric Atlas is a 1.9 m, 90 kg biped with 56 DoF, official industrial reach claims, and public demonstrations of standing, walking, and whole-body movement.
caveats: No walking speed, obstacle-course, fall-rate, or long-duration mobility benchmark was found.
Some public videos are edited company demos.
CES stage mobility should be treated as remote-piloted demo evidence.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Official materials claim a 360-degree camera, tactile sensing, human detection for fenceless operation, and behavior generation from 2D/3D vision-model inputs.
caveats: No perception benchmark, confusion matrix, or safety-validation report was found.
Sensor and software descriptions are company claims.
Human detection claims are not equivalent to certified collaborative-robot safety evidence.

human_interaction.summary: Evidence is mostly industrial safety/operator workflow claims: teach/intent-selection modes, remote operation, human detection, and fenceless-operation positioning.
caveats: No natural-language, social-interaction, or human-subject evaluation was found.
Operator modes are not proof of unsupervised human collaboration.
No third-party safety certification evidence was found.

endurance_reliability.summary: Official specs claim 4 hr runtime, swappable 1.4 kWh battery, IP67 ingress rating, -20 C to 55 C operation, and serviceability features.
caveats: Runtime and environmental ratings are official claims, not independently audited in reviewed sources.
No MTBF, uptime, fleet operating-hours, or maintenance-cost data was found.
A 4 hr battery spec does not prove full-shift continuous production reliability.

human_environment_fit.summary: Boston Dynamics frames Atlas as a human-form robot for human-centered industrial spaces, with claimed reach, payload, and station compatibility for automotive and logistics tasks.
caveats: No independent workstation-fit study was found.
Human-environment fit is inferred from industrial task framing and dimensions.
No public evidence shows broad household or unstructured public-space use.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Boston Dynamics says the first customer deployment is complete and that 2026 deployments with Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind are committed; AP reports Hyundai plans factory deployment by 2028.
caveats: Customer deployment details and volumes are not independently published.
Hyundai and Google DeepMind evidence is mostly company/partner roadmap evidence, not fleet performance data.
No price, open purchasing route, or paid-customer case study was found.

accessibility_value.summary: No public price, open purchase path, accessibility use case, or affordability evidence was found; product is positioned for enterprise industrial deployments.
caveats: No price was found.
No public waitlist or consumer availability was found.
Industrial enterprise positioning limits accessibility scoring.

evidence_items.title: Official Atlas product specs
evidence_items.claim: Boston Dynamics lists Electric Atlas as a 1.9 m, 90 kg, 56-DoF industrial humanoid with 50 kg payload, 4 hr runtime, 1.4 kWh swappable battery, IP67 rating, 360-degree camera, and tactile gripper.
evidence_items.notes: Official specification evidence; not independently measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Backfills concrete physical, battery, sensor, and manipulation specs for arena scoring.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Height: 1.9 m; Weight: 90 kg; Payload: 50 kg; Runtime: 4 hr; Degrees of freedom: 56; Battery: 1.4 kWh; Ingress protection: IP67.
evidence_items.source_location: Atlas product page and Atlas Spec Sheet, Specifications tables
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official Boston Dynamics sources agree on core specs; treat as company-provided specs, not audited measurements.

evidence_items.title: Operating modes and industrial task positioning
evidence_items.claim: The Atlas spec sheet describes autonomous operation alongside teach, teleoperation, intent selection, and policy learning, and lists use cases including automotive part sequencing, machine tending, palletizing, and order fulfillment.
evidence_items.notes: Useful for task scope and operating-mode evidence, but does not quantify autonomous success rates.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Supports industrial-task scoring while preserving the distinction between autonomous, operator-assisted, and teleoperated modes.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Operation Modes: Autonomous, Teach, Teleoperation, Intent Selection, Policy Learning. Applications: Part Sequencing; Machine Tending; Material Handling; Order Fulfillment.
evidence_items.source_location: Atlas Spec Sheet, Operation Modes and Applications
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company claim only; no independent benchmark or task-log evidence found.

evidence_items.title: Electric Atlas public introduction
evidence_items.claim: Boston Dynamics introduced a fully electric Atlas and said it was designed for real-world applications, following retirement of the hydraulic Atlas platform.
evidence_items.notes: Announcement evidence establishes lineage and first public date, not deployed capability.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Corrects announcement timing and distinguishes Electric Atlas from the prior hydraulic research platform.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The next generation of the Atlas program builds on decades of research and furthers our commitment to delivering the most capable, useful mobile robots.
evidence_items.source_location: Boston Dynamics blog, electric Atlas announcement
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official announcement; no independent performance data in the announcement.

evidence_items.title: Product-version Atlas and committed 2026 deployments
evidence_items.claim: Boston Dynamics says the production-ready Atlas entered immediate manufacturing and that all 2026 deployments are already committed, including to Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind.
evidence_items.notes: Strong company deployment signal, but not independent fleet-performance proof.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Supports higher deployment confidence than a pure prototype, while remaining below independently documented commercial operation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The product version of Atlas is here, with production beginning immediately. All deployments in 2026 have already been committed, including initial recipients Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official Boston Dynamics launch claim; volumes, contract terms, and live operating metrics were not public.

evidence_items.title: First customer deployment and Hyundai field-testing context
evidence_items.claim: Boston Dynamics says Atlas completed its first customer deployment in the prior year and is taking its first steps into a customer facility at Hyundai's Georgia Metaplant.
evidence_items.notes: Customer facility language is important, but details remain sparse and primarily company-sourced.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Adds deployment context beyond demo videos, but without sufficient metrics for commercial-production scoring.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: After having completed our first customer deployment last year, we're excited to be taking our first steps into a customer facility with Atlas.
evidence_items.source_location: Boston Dynamics Enterprise Robotics CES 2026 article; Atlas product page deployment section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official source; no customer-authored case study, fleet count, uptime, or task-completion statistics found.

evidence_items.title: CES demo was remotely piloted
evidence_items.claim: AP reported that Boston Dynamics' live CES presentation showed Atlas walking out, jumping, and lifting a box, but that the robot was being remotely piloted.
evidence_items.notes: Credible media context materially limits autonomy credit for the public stage demo.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Prevents over-crediting a public demo as autonomous task execution.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: During a live presentation, a remote-piloted Atlas walked out and did a little jump before lifting up a box.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Credible media report; not a raw technical audit, but directly addresses teleoperation status of the demo.

evidence_items.title: Perception and learning stack direction
evidence_items.claim: Boston Dynamics describes work toward Atlas behavior generation from vision models, including 2D and 3D foundation-model inputs and real-time robot adaptation.
evidence_items.notes: Architecture and roadmap evidence, not a finished benchmark.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Adds credible perception/autonomy context without overclaiming deployed capability.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: We're using both 2D and 3D vision foundation models as inputs to generate our behavior, and robot learning to adjust these motions in real time.
evidence_items.source_location: Boston Dynamics Atlas evolution blog, software section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official technical narrative; no reproducible benchmark or dataset released in reviewed source.

deployments.customer: Hyundai RMAC / Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America
deployments.description: Boston Dynamics says 2026 deployments are committed, including Hyundai RMAC, and product-page language says Atlas is taking its first steps into a customer facility at Hyundai's Georgia Metaplant.
deployments.notes: No public fleet size, duty cycle, uptime, task-success rate, or customer-authored case study found.

deployments.description: Boston Dynamics says Google DeepMind is an initial 2026 recipient of product-version Atlas deployments.
deployments.notes: Deployment appears research/partner-oriented from public evidence; no operating metrics found.

demos.title: CES 2026 public Atlas demo
demos.editing_notes: AP described a live presentation, but this update did not manually review full raw footage.
demos.teleoperation_notes: AP described the CES Atlas demo as remote-piloted, so it should not be credited as autonomous task execution.
caveats: Remote-piloted demo evidence is useful for physical mobility/manipulation context, not autonomy scoring.
No raw task log, repeat count, failure count, or intervention count was published.

observed_segments.observation: AP reported that Atlas walked out, jumped, and lifted a box during a remote-piloted live presentation.
observed_segments.verification_notes: Media-reported observation; timestamp not verified in this update.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Official sources claim autonomous modes and learning-based behavior generation, but no independent autonomy benchmark, intervention rate, or raw production task log was found. AP says the CES stage demo was remotely piloted.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Give limited autonomy credit for official industrial-pilot claims; do not score public CES motion as autonomous.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Boston Dynamics reports a first customer deployment and committed 2026 recipients, but no customer-authored case study, fleet count, uptime, or paid-commercial terms were found.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Score above prototype-only robots, but below robots with independently documented sustained commercial operation.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Runtime, IP67, and environmental operating range are official specs; no MTBF, maintenance interval, fall rate, or production uptime evidence was found.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Use endurance specs as moderate evidence, not proof of full-shift industrial reliability.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No public price, open purchase path, or general commercial availability was found.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Do not award accessibility or market-availability credit beyond enterprise pilot/deployment status.

excluded_claims.reason: Reviewed sources do not independently verify broad autonomy.

excluded_claims.claim: Independent benchmark across all arena dimensions
excluded_claims.reason: No full independent benchmark was found.
AP reported the live CES demo was remotely piloted.
Reviewed sources show enterprise positioning and committed recipients, not open purchase availability or price.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Electric Atlas now has strong company-source evidence for industrial specs, production-version launch, committed 2026 deployments, and Hyundai customer-facility field testing, but public autonomy evidence remains weak because no independent benchmarks or operating metrics were found and AP reported the CES 2026 stage demo was remotely piloted.
strongest_evidence: Official specs: 1.9 m, 90 kg, 56 DoF, 50 kg payload, 4 hr runtime, 1.4 kWh swappable battery, IP67 rating, tactile gripper, and 360-degree camera.
Boston Dynamics says product-version Atlas production began immediately and all 2026 deployments are committed, including Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind.
Boston Dynamics says Atlas completed a first customer deployment and is entering a Hyundai Metaplant customer facility.
weakest_evidence: No independent arena benchmark, uptime, task-success rate, failure rate, or intervention rate.
CES 2026 stage demo was reported as remotely piloted, limiting autonomy credit.
No public price, open purchase path, or customer-authored deployment metrics.
known_do_not_credit: Remote-piloted CES demo as autonomous performance.
General consumer or open commercial availability.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Strong official spec and deployment-roadmap evidence; still weak for independent autonomy, reliability, and commercial performance metrics.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official Atlas specs now include 1.9 m height, 90 kg weight, 56 DoF, 50 kg instant payload, 30 kg sustained payload, 4 hr battery life, 1.4 kWh swappable battery, IP67 rating, tactile sensing, and 360-degree camera view.
Boston Dynamics says the product version is being manufactured and all 2026 deployments are committed, including Hyundai RMAC and Google DeepMind.
Boston Dynamics says Hyundai is the first customer, with a completed deployment last year and a fleet scheduled for RMAC in 2026.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No independent autonomy benchmark or arena-style evaluation.
No intervention, failure-rate, uptime, MTBF, fleet-hours, or task-success metrics.
No public price, broad availability, or customer-authored production case study.
AP reports the CES 2026 stage demo was remote-piloted, so it should not be credited as autonomous evidence.
conflicting_claims: Boston Dynamics describes autonomous operation and minimal supervision, while AP reports the high-profile CES live demo was remotely piloted; treat the demo as teleoperated and the autonomy claims as company roadmap/product claims until benchmarked.
do_not_overclaim: Independent benchmark across all arena dimensions
CES 2026 public demo as autonomous proof
Generally purchasable robot or known price
